caption: Two half adders stacked: the bottom one adds A and B, and its sum climbs a redstone dust to the top one, which adds the carry-in and gives the sum. Each half adder lights its own carry block, and the carry-out lamp sits between the two blocks, so it lights when either carry does. A glass block above the bottom carry torch keeps that torch from lighting the lamp.

A torch on input A and input B's wire meet in a comparator that is fully on when both are off, barely on when only B is on, and off when A is on. The carry lights when B is on and that comparator is off (both inputs on); the sum lights when exactly one input is on. Found by a SAT search.

Each bit is two half adders side by side: each half adder's carry feeds a repeater, the two lines join, and a last repeater lights a lamp that is the next bit's carry-in. Copies stacked every 7 blocks make a ripple-carry adder of any width (judged at 1 to 4 and 8 bits).
